H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper describes a flat sequential loop: start, convey package, stop at sensor, fill/count, resume conveyor. No parent mode, nested substate, or composite state is specified.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions are guarded by Start, Stop, photoelectric container detection, proximity pulse detection, and the count reaching the HMI setting; the key guard is equivalent to present_count >= hmi_setpoint.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: The controller stops/starts the conveyor, starts/stops the reservoir motor, increments the counter from proximity pulses, and displays the present counter value on the HMI.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: A Stop button is described as turning off system work and stopping the process, but the paper gives no fault state, recovery path, or explicit safe-state semantics.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: The main process sequence is in Work Description, while later sections define sensor pulse semantics, PLC I/O addresses, motor output behavior, and HMI counter setting/display.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as HMI, counter, photoelectric sensor, and proximity sensor are accompanied by explicit behavior rules; no unstated interlock, fail-safe, or recovery rule must be decoded.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The core actions are stated in the same process prose as the transition conditions; later sections refine implementation details rather than relocating state actions away from a separate state definition.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The fill-complete transition depends on the counted steel balls matching the HMI-entered setting value, i.e., a guard comparing present_count with hmi_setpoint.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite state or parent-state entry/during/exit behavior is present.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The Stop button is a normal operator control; the paper does not declare an any-state fault-to-safe transition or layered recovery rule.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite state, initial pseudostate chain, or nested mode routing is described.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There is one meaningful data guard comparing the accumulated counter against the HMI setpoint; other guards are simple input events.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The Stop button plausibly cuts across the active conveying/filling loop, but the paper does not state a broad any-state fault or monitor rule.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The HMI present-value counter is a monitoring/status output, but most side effects are concrete PLC motor outputs.

key_nl_quotes: conveyor will stop when the container/package is detected
according to the setting value counter/number of products entered in the HMI
one_line_pitch: A compact PLC/HMI EFSM where the modeler must recover count-vs-setpoint guards, sensor-pulse counter updates, motor side effects, and an operator stop from process prose split across the paper.
rationale: This is a meaningful stress case for guard and action extraction because the central behavior depends on a configurable HMI setpoint, pulse-count updates, and coordinated motor outputs. It is not a top candidate because the machine is essentially flat and lacks real hierarchy, fault recovery, or deep cross-cutting semantics. It remains useful as a backup sample for testing whether a baseline can turn industrial PLC prose into an EFSM rather than a pure event list.
